title: Economic Expansion Incentives (Relief from Income Tax) (Amendment) Bill
what_it_is: Economic Expansion Incentives (Relief from Income Tax) (Amendment) Bill

sections.label: IP income excluded from incentives
sections.summary: IP income is removed from the Pioneer Service Companies and Development and Expansion Incentive schemes, which grant tax exemption or concessionary rates on qualifying activity income.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
sentences.text: The first change is to exclude Intellectual Property Income from Pioneer Service Companies, and Development and Expansion Incentive.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
sentences.text: Accordingly, IP income will be removed from the scope of the Pioneer Service Companies (PSCs) and Development and Expansion Incentive (DEI) schemes, which currently provide for tax exemption or concessionary tax rates respectively on income from qualifying activities, which may include IP income.

sections.label: IIA scheme liberalised and extended
sections.summary: The IIA scheme will require qualifying equipment to be primarily used for the approved project by the overseas company, and is extended to 31 December 2022.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
sentences.text: As announced in Budget 2017, this will be liberalised to only require the qualifying equipment to be primarily used for the approved project by the overseas company.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
sentences.text: In addition, the IIA scheme will be extended till 31 December 2022.

sections.label: Why IP income undefined
sections.summary: The passage asks the Minister to clarify why the meaning of IP Income is not specifically defined within the Bill.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Can the Minister clarify why the meaning of IP Income is not specifically defined within the Bill?

sections.label: Defining IP income and IDI fit
sections.summary: The passage asks whether a clear definition of IP Income will be included in the Bill and how clause 5's IP income exclusion fits the EDB-administered IDI regime.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: To my mind, it is a tenuous argument to rely on flexibility to justify why the definition of an important term, such as IP Income, should be left to the Minister to prescribe.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Hence, will the Minister consider including a specific clear definition of IP Income within the Bill?

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Second, can the Minister clarify how the amendments relating to the exclusion of IP income as stated in clause 5 of the Bill fit into the new IP regime administered by EDB, named IDI announced during the 2017 Singapore Budget?

sections.label: Data on MNCs and managers
sections.summary: The passage asks the Minister for three years of data on foreign MNCs with regional offices enjoying tax incentives and the percentage of Singaporeans in managerial positions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Can the Minister provide data over the past three years on the relationship between the number of foreign MNCs with a regional office in Singapore which are enjoying such tax incentives and the percentage of Singaporeans in managerial positions in these MNCs?

sections.label: SME benefit from PC amendments
sections.summary: The passage asks whether SMEs can benefit from the amendments, noting only two of 71 PCs went to SMEs between 2011 and 2015.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: From the Minister's reply in 2016, I understand that for the current PC Incentive scheme, between 2011 and 2015, only two out of 71 PCs were awarded to SMEs, of which only one was a local SME.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The explanation then was that PC application requires companies to commit to economic contributions of a substantive scale.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Keeping in mind that the principle behind this Bill and the Act is to put in place tax incentives to encourage innovation, I wish to ask whether there are ways in which our SMEs can benefit from these amendments.

sections.label: Tax incentives and big companies
sections.summary: A Member asks how structuring tax incentives for bigger companies fits the Bill's principles, noting only two SMEs got final certificates between 2011 and 2015.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: If we are structuring the tax incentives to largely allow for bigger companies to meet the criteria, can the Minister clarify how this is in line with the principles of the Bill?

sentences.speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: As mentioned by Minister Lim Hng Kiang, between 2011 and 2015, similar companies had been awarded final certificates, of which, only two were SMEs, which is of concern to me.

sections.label: Removal of prescribed IP income
sections.summary: The removal of prescribed IP income from the tax incentives schemes of Pioneer Service Companies and Development and Expansion Companies is questioned.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The removal of the prescribed IP Income from the tax incentives scheme of both Pioneer Service Companies and Development and Expansion Companies under Part III section 19A and Part IIIB section 19M are questionable.

sections.label: Concern over smaller companies
sections.summary: A Member says larger companies and larger SMEs may absorb the change but is concerned about smaller ones that could not capitalise on incentive schemes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: While this change may be able to get absorbed by larger companies like the PSCs and larger-sized SMEs, I am very concerned over smaller ones which have not been able to capitalise on incentive schemes.

sections.label: Bill excludes IP income
sections.summary: The Bill amends the legislation to exclude IP income from PSC and DEI companies to align with international standards and BEPS guidelines.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Hng Kiang
sentences.text: To be in line with international standards and, in particular, to align ourselves with BEPS guidelines, this Bill will, therefore, amend the legislation to exclude IP income from PSC and DEI companies.

sections.label: IDI consultation and legislation
sections.summary: The Government is consulting companies on IDI, and the incentive will be legislated in the Income Tax Act.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Hng Kiang
sentences.text: As for IDI itself, the Government is currently in consultation with companies and the incentive will be legislated in the Income Tax Act consequently.

sections.label: LIUP expanded to PACT scheme
sections.summary: The LIUP scheme caters to local SMEs supplying multinationals or large companies, and has been expanded to the PACT scheme covering collaborations beyond supplier relationships.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Hng Kiang
sentences.text: As Members would remember, the LIUP scheme essentially caters to the relationship of our local SMEs who are suppliers to the multinational or the large companies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Hng Kiang
sentences.text: But we think the relationship can go beyond that of just a supplier relationship and, therefore, we have expanded the LIUP scheme to the PACT scheme which encompasses different forms of collaborations and partnerships, beyond just a supplier relationship.
